51602951.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to apo PRMT5 (1 to 637 residues)(unknown origin) expressed in baculovirus infected Sf21 insect cells assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: PRMT5 SPR (surface plasmon resonance) binding assays were carried out in the presence of either PRMT5 methylation cofactor SAM (S-adenosyl methionine), MTA, or no ligand (i.e., apo form of PRMT5) to complement the MOI information gathered from the biochemical assay approach and to provide orthogonal validation for hits, i.e., to show that hit compounds were genuine PRMT5 protein binders. Representative hits were also profiled in in vitro ADME assays and submitted for X-ray crystallography using co-crystals of the PRMT5–MTA complex to provide valuable structural information from an early stage. PRMT5-specific cellular assays were developed to profile representatives of HTS hits. A symmetrical dimethyl arginine methylation (SDMA) cellular imaging assay was developed to provide a quantification of the cellular inhibition of PRMT5 through measurement of the specific symmetrical dimethyl arginine methylation marks specific to PRMT5 activity on histone and non-histone substrates. These assays were set using a two-dimensional cultured isogenic matched pair of HCT-116 colon cell lines in which one of the two lines has the MTAP gene removed ("MTAP KO") using CRISPR knockout techniques and the other line has the MTAP gene retained ("MTAP WT"). During chemistry hit finding and optimization, the goal was to optimize compounds toward maximum cellular SDMA inhibition potency in the MTAP KO cell line and the minimum possible inhibition of SDMA in the MTAP WT cell line setting, with the fold ratio between MTAP WT and MTAP KO potency IC50's defining the fold "MTA cooperativity" [(MTAP WT IC50)/(MTAP KO IC50)].
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Figure 5. Profiling of HTS hit 1 to demonstrate its MTA-cooperative mode of inhibition and ADME properties. (A) Structure of 1 and biochemical PRMT5 potency (note that the PRMT5 biochemical assays were reconfigured for SAR screening after HTS; in Figure 4, compound 1 in these HTS biochemical assays has IC50's of X nM with MTA and X nM with no MTA). (B) SPR sensorgrams of 1 with PRMT5 in the presence of no cofactor, MTA, or SAM (C) Representative concentration response curves for 1 in cell SDMA inhibition assays (HCT-116 MTAP KO and MTAP WT) showing MTA-cooperative inhibition. (D) In vitro ADME data for 1. aMeasured log D at pH7.4. bSolubility of compounds in aqueous phosphate buffer at pH7.4 after 24 h at 25 °C. cDetermined from a dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) stock solution by equilibrium dialysis in 10% rat plasma. dRate of metabolism (microliters per minute per 106 cells) determined from a DMSO stock solution in isolated hepatocytes diluted to 1 × 106 cells/mL. eCompounds were incubated at 10 μM in cultured Caco-2 cells. Permeability was measured in units of ×10−6 cm/s in the apical to basolateral (A to B) direction in the presence of inhibitors preventing basolateral to apical (B to A) efflux. fThe efflux ratio is expressed as (Papp B to A)/(Papp A to B) in the uninhibited form of the assay.
original_paragraph.Figure 5B: The SPR sensorgrams in Figure 5B show the response over time for compound 1 binding to PRMT5 under three conditions: Apo (no cofactor), +MTA, and +SAM. The x-axis is Time (s) ranging from 0 to 1500. The y-axis is Response (RU). The curves are labeled with their respective dissociation constants (Kd): Apo (Kd 1.3 μM), +MTA (Kd 1.0 nM), and +SAM (Kd 6.3 nM). The +MTA curve shows a much higher response and slower dissociation compared to the Apo and +SAM curves, indicating stronger binding in the presence of MTA.

51602953.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to apo PRMT5 (1 to 637 residues)(unknown origin) expressed in baculovirus infected Sf21 insect cells using SAM as substrate assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: SPR binding assays were performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) using a CM5 sensor chip. PRMT5 (1–637) was immobilized on the chip via amine coupling. The running buffer was 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.005% P20, 0.01% BSA. Compounds were diluted in running buffer and injected at concentrations ranging from 0.1 nM to 10 μM. The association phase was 120 s, and the dissociation phase was 180 s. Regeneration was achieved with 10 mM glycine, pH 2.0. Data were analyzed using Biacore Evaluation Software 3.0. The dissociation constant (Kd) was determined by fitting the sensorgrams to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model.
